extracted.intended_audience: state adjutants general, War Department legal and finance officers, and attorneys/administrators handling militia appropriations, leases, and target-range matters
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and administrative standards governing use of appropriations, leases, liabilities, transportation, and target-range acquisition and operation for the Organized Militia/National Guard where they interact with the Regular Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied contract for reasonable compensation for use and occupancy
rubrics_metrics.description: When lands are used as quartermaster and commissary depots under conditions indicating an understanding between proprietor and quartermaster that the lands were to be so used for a reasonable compensation, there is an implied contract for a reasonable compensation for the use and occupancy for that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leases executed after the occupancy period may be treated as a liquidation of the claim for use and compensation. (C.16525, Nov.16,1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of leases made after the occupancy period
rubrics_metrics.description: Leases for a period made out after the period of occupancy (ineffectual to create an actual term) may nevertheless be treated as a liquidation of the claim for use and compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such post-period leases as evidence of agreed compensation for the earlier use. (C.16525, Nov.16,1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking of militia officers when serving with Regular Army
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Organized Militia and the Regular Army serve together as contemplated by statutes, the one hundred and twenty-fourth article of war requires that no officer of the militia of a particular grade can rank any Regular officer of that grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where militia and Regulars serve together under section 9 of the act of May 27, 1908 amending section 15 of Jan 21, 1903. (C.14148-F, Sept.12,1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'participation' with Regular Army
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Participation' in encampment, maneuvers, and field instruction begins when the movement from the several rendezvous begins and ends when troops reach their respective rendezvous on return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this period the militia are entitled to the same pay, subsistence, and transportation as Regular Army troops. (C.14148, Aug.4,1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement of joint encampment appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation sums provided in annual Army support acts for joint encampments of Regular Army and Organized Militia cannot lawfully be transferred to a disbursing officer of a State; they must be disbursed by regularly appointed officers of the staff departments of the Regular Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State disbursing officers should not be used to expend these specific federal appropriations. (C.14148-F, July 1,1908 & Dec.13,1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation procurement for militia when participating
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 15 of Jan.21,1903, transportation for militia forces to and from maneuvers on a military reservation must be obtained in the same way and pursuant to the same statutes and regulations as for corresponding detachments of the Regular Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Regular Army procurement statutes/regulations for transportation of militia when they 'participate.' (C.14148-S, Sept.11,1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-authority to charge automobile hire for certain militia staff to joint encampment appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: If certain staff officers of the Organized Militia were not designated by the Secretary of War to take part in the joint encampment, hiring an automobile for their transportation from the State capital to the joint encampment does not constitute a lawful charge against the appropriation for the joint encampment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only travel/transportation for those authorized to participate may be charged. (C.14148-H, Sept.6,1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale of subsistence stores to militia at cost prices
rubrics_metrics.description: At a joint encampment, subsistence stores sold to officers and enlisted men of the Organized Militia who participate should be sold at cost prices, i.e., the same prices charged to officers and enlisted men of the Regular Army under the same circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure parity of pricing between militia participants and Regular troops. (C.14148, Aug.5,1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Forage not allowed under section 15 participation allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 15 of Jan.21,1903 restricts allowances to 'pay, subsistence, and transportation' for the National Guard participating with the Regular Army; forage is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include forage as an allowance under that statutory participation provision. (C.14148, July 13,1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor allowances incident to rations may be issued
rubrics_metrics.description: When rations are furnished to the National Guard under section 15, Army Regulations permit issuing fuel for cooking purposes (used to cook the ration) and hay for bedding as minor allowances probably included in the substantial allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat fuel for cooking and hay for bedding as incidental to rations when militia participate with Regular Army. (C.14148, Sept.12,1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriation for purchase of subsistence and employment of civilians
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation clause 'For purchase of subsistence and supplies, one hundred thousand dollars' in connection with joint encampments is broad enough to authorize employing civilians to bake bread under the same circumstances as for Regular troops, and to pay for ordinary labor necessary for handling subsistence stores in a maneuver camp composed of both Regulars and Volunteers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay for such labor should be made from the appropriation for subsistence of the Army and the subsistence of the militia in proportion to the strength of Regular and militia forces. (C.16524, July/Aug 1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bakery profits are not pay or allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Bakery profits are neither pay nor allowances; a militia organization participating in an encampment at an Army post for less than 10 days under section 15 is not entitled to share in the bakery savings of the post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat bakery savings as compensation to participating militia units for short durations. (C.14148-E, May/June 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: State militia officers cannot contract obligations without War Department authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers of a State National Guard cannot contract bills for transportation, labor, material, or similar items at their discretion without reference to or authority of the proper bureau of the War Department for payment under section 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts incuring obligations for payment from federal appropriations require War Department authority. (C.14148, Oct.28/Dec.18,1903 & Jan.28,1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital expenses incurred after breaking of camp not payable from US funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If a private of the National Guard placed in a civil hospital due to sickness cannot accompany his regiment home, hospital expenses incurred after the breaking of camp cannot be paid from United States funds in the hands of the disbursing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such post-camp medical bills are not chargeable to federal militia funds. (C.14148-D, Oct.3/14,1907.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation covers damages naturally and necessarily arising from use of leased lands
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation for 'transportation of the militia and its supplies, do tiling, and equipage, lease of land, and damage to property' must provide for payment of damages naturally and necessarily arising out of the use of lands leased for military maneuvers (e.g., damage to growing crops, fences, detached buildings, inclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theft, larceny, wanton destruction, or injuries not susceptible of liquidation as described are not payable out of the appropriation; tortious acts of individuals cannot be paid from Congressional appropriations and should be adjusted by the States or by claimants to Congress or Court of Claims. (C.16525, May 19,1904; C.14971, July 23/Aug 28,1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for use of unleased lands during maneuvers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where troops enter parcels not subject to leases and claims are made for rent and injury, rent claims should be rejected but claims for injury to crops and fences, after adjustment, should be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation for physical injury to property used in maneuvers may be allowed even absent a lease; rent for unleased occupancy generally is not allowed. (C.16525, Nov.3,1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations cannot be used to adjust unliquidated damages absent contract
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department cannot pay claims for loss of equipment (e.g., railway baggage car loss) or other unliquidated damages unless express provision is made by contract to cover such adjustment; lost equipment may not be a legitimate part of the cost of transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require contractual provision for liability adjustments; otherwise such claims are not payable. (C.14971, July 29,1904; 20402, Sept.26,1906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: United States not responsible for unlawful acts (torts) of soldiers or militia
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States is not legally responsible for the unlawful acts or torts of its soldiers, officers, agents, or the Organized Militia; the remedy is suit against individuals, application to Congress, or recourse to the State whose troops committed the acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive departments cannot lawfully compensate individuals for torts committed by State militia; any contract purporting to bind the US for such payments would be without operative force. (C.16525, May 19,1904; C.17585, Feb.27,1905; C.16961, Oct.1,1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure authority for improvements to government-designated rifle ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: If a quarter section of public domain has been withdrawn from entry and set apart for use as a rifle range, no further action is necessary as a condition to the expenditure of money in improvement of the range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds may be expended to improve officially withdrawn public lands used as ranges. (C.19798, Aug.1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and trustee relation for lands purchased under section 1661
rubrics_metrics.description: Title to lands purchased under section 1661, R.S., as amended, for use as State target ranges vests in the United States; the State or Territory is a trustee charged with administration for the purpose for which acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter into contracts binding the United States for purchases from future appropriations; after Attorney General approval of title, payment and recording may proceed. (C.19798; C.20864.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable charges to State allotment for acquiring target ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: From a State's allotment under section 1661 the following expenses are allowable if acquisition is consummated: (1) travel to secure an option; (2) expenses in securing owner consent to sell; (3) preparation of title for Attorney General submission; (4) necessary surveys; (5) purchase price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses for surveying proposed ranges and obtaining options that were not later required, and payment for options, are not properly charged. (C.19798, Dec.29,1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Leasing target-range grounds and adaptation expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Renting grounds for target ranges or buildings for shooting galleries, together with expenses necessarily attending their adaptation for instruction in small-arms firing, are proper subjects for expenditure under section 1661 and related acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of the Governor of the State is required for leases under the act of June 22,1906; Secretary of War approval not required for such leases unless an option to purchase is exercised. (C.14148-B; P.20989, Apr.1907; C.20989, July 5,1907.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of title and lease formality for long-term leases
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term leases where rental is paid in advance, the lease should be properly executed, acknowledged, recorded, and evidence furnished of lessor's title so the Government is assured of occupancy for the paid term; for year-to-year or less-than-five-year leases with year-to-year rental, evidence of title is not usually required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property description should identify the land but need not be as exact as a conveyance; signatures witnessing lessor preferred though not always necessary; leases without title evidence should not stipulate rental paid in advance. (C.20989, June 1909; Jan/Apr/May 1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease should state purpose and terms for target-range use
rubrics_metrics.description: A lease of land for use as a target range should show the purpose for which the premises are leased and, if long-term with prepaid rental, include conditions addressing future appropriations or year-to-year continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no funds exist for entire period, insert stipulation that continuance beyond one year conditioned on future appropriations; lessee option to terminate (e.g., 90 days notice) permissible. (G.20989; G.21506.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use following ambiguous description may validate lease use
rubrics_metrics.description: If property description is not precise but a certain 'strip of land' answering to the description is used for target-range purposes during the specified period, the lease followed by such use may be regarded as sufficient for the purpose in view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases rent should not be paid in advance. (G.20989-A, Apr.1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and subsistence expenses for officers in range acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the Organized Militia who travels under competent orders in connection with acquisition and development of target ranges is entitled to actual expenses for travel and subsistence out of the funds allotted under section 1661, R.S., as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge officer travel/subsistence to the State allotment when travel is under competent orders. (C.14148-E; C.19798.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance premiums only chargeable if lease requires insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lease for a target range provides that buildings should be insured, the expenditure for taking out insurance is proper and the policy should be kept with lease papers; if the lease contains no provision requiring lessee to insure, payment of premiums is not a proper charge against the appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat insurance premium as part of consideration only when contractually required. (C.20989, Apr.1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Forage for State-purchased animals not chargeable to section 1661 funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If a team of mules was purchased out of State funds for use on a State rifle range, there is no authority to issue forage purchased from funds accruing under section 1661, R.S.; necessary forage must be purchased from State funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish purchases made with State funds vs. federal allotments for operational consumables. (C.14148-G, Dec.1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Well and water supply improvements chargeable to allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is necessary to dig a well and equip it with pump and tanks to render a range suitable (for presence of water for fire and men), necessary expenses connected therewith are proper charges against the State's apportionment under the appropriation for promotion of rifle practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements essential to safe operation of range are allowable charges. (C.19798, July 1907.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputes affecting use of leased range are State matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If a private claims a prescriptive right to run a road that would interfere with range operations, although Federal appropriation pays rental, the lease is entered by the State and the matter should be handled by State authorities in State courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal allotment payment does not convert lease disputes into War Department jurisdiction. (C.21506, Oct.30,1907.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Board membership to adjudicate damage claims under leases
rubrics_metrics.description: Leases for target practice purposes usually stipulate that one member of a claims board shall be appointed by the lessor, one by the lessee, and the third by those two; their finding is final when approved by the disbursing officer or some general officer of the militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such arbitration/board provisions in leases to provide an agreed method for liquidating damage claims. (C.20989-A, Apr.28,1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for adaptation-damage under lease are legitimate charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a lease provides payment of 'damages done as specified to crops and all other property on said premises,' a claim for value of fruit trees destroyed or removed to adapt premises is a legitimate claim against funds placed to credit of the disbursing officer under section 1661.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document adaptation actions and claim amounts; such claims are proper if within lease provisions. (C.20989, May 1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Leasing/pasturing Government-owned range land
rubrics_metrics.description: Land purchased with Congressional appropriations for militia rifle range use (title in US) may be leased for pasture under conditions not interfering with range use; rent belongs to the United States and must be deposited to miscellaneous receipts, though adjutant general may authorize revocable license with conditions requiring betterments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat rents as federal receipts; use revocable license when adjutant general permits incidental uses. (C.26465, Apr.1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation coverage for promotion of rifle practice and inspectors
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of June 22, 1906 makes provision for promotion of rifle practice; that appropriation covers payment of salary and expenses of inspectors engaged in promoting rifle practice within a State (except during encampment/maneuvers etc., when other appropriations apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appropriation will not cover certain yearly payments to officers/enlisted men required by State law (e.g., per-shot payments). Incidental expenses of rifle matches (pay of men working targets, prizes) become proper charges only if the Secretary of War has favorably exercised discretion to make them part of the promotion allotment. (C.20168, Aug.8,1906; July 15,1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: State team members entitled to pay/subsistence/transportation for competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of teams (e.g., five-man teams from companies) at State-ordered target competitions is 'actual field or camp service for instruction' and members are entitled to pay, subsistence, and transportation under the statute; transportation and subsistence for State teams at national competitions may be paid from funds accruing to the State under section 1661 and section 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each man selected from different companies is entitled to pay/transportation/subsistence from date of leaving his company's station. Commutation of rations at Army Regulation rates is a proper charge. When attending the national match, enlisted men's subsistence during the match is defrayed from Army support; prior matches' subsistence comes from State allotment; commissioned officers must subsist themselves. (C.14148-B; C.14148-A; C.14148-G.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and funding limits for State teams and spectators
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations classed as reserve militia not part of the National Guard do not receive funds under section 1661 and members are not eligible to serve on State rifle teams for national matches; spectators (e.g., five officers as spectators) accompanying State teams cannot be allowed transportation, pay, or subsistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure team membership and reimbursable travel are limited to eligible Organized Militia/National Guard members. (C.19798; C.14148-A, June 3,1905.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'year' in statutory prerequisite to allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 18 requires activities during 'the year next preceding each annual allotment'—the word 'year' refers to a calendar year, not a fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calendar-year compliance when documenting prerequisite drills, inspections, and practices for allotment eligibility. (C.14148, May 20,1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation/storage costs chargeable to rifle-practice appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of transportation of freight of target supplies from the State arsenal to various ranges, storage of equipment pending lease completion, and dray charges from storage to installation are proper charges against the appropriation for promotion of rifle practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these logistical costs when charging the State allotment under section 1661. (C.14148-F, Apr.16,1909; C.14148-C, Feb.9,1907.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation of new material issued by staff departments
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of transporting new material and supplies issued by staff departments to the Organized Militia is borne by the United States and paid out of 'Transportation of the Army.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return transportation from State armories to depots/arsenals cannot be paid from 'Transportation of the Army.' Items rendered unserviceable by fair wear and tear must be transported at the cost of the State to which issued; repairs from accident or fair wear cannot be cleanly differentiated from neglect in determining payment of transportation. (See multiple Comptroller opinions cited: C.14148-G; C.1455.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular Army appropriations not available for militia joint encampment expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of April 23,1904 forbids payment of expenses of the Organized Militia in joint encampment with the Regular Army out of funds appropriated for the Regular Army; act of June 12,1906 limits expenditures for militia participating in joint encampments to the period from leaving the home rendezvous to return thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States cannot be reimbursed from Regular Army appropriations for certain militia expenses (e.g., freight on blankets/ponchos shipped from State arsenal to company stations). Use appropriate militia-specific allotments. (C.14148-C, Feb.15,1907.)
